extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and stakeholders involved in PTAB proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: An overview of PTAB functions, ex parte appeals, and AIA trial proceedings (IPR/PGR/Derivation), including who may file, timelines, possible outcomes, sources of law, common motions, and PTAB priorities. Intended as guidance for practitioners and parties interacting with PTAB processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB definition and role
rubrics_metrics.description: A neutral administrative adjudicatory body (known as the “Board”) within the United States Patent and Trademark Office; created on September 16, 2012, by the America Invents Act (AIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background/history: previously the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (BPAI); the Board has a long history back to 1861. Establishes that PTAB is an internal adjudicatory forum for patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who issues decisions at the PTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions are issued by just under 200 administrative patent judges (APJs) located in 5 different offices nationwide and four statutory members (Director, Deputy Director, Commissioner for Patents, Commissioner for Trademarks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All APJs are both legally and technically trained with extensive experience in patent law (law firms, in-house, DOJ, USPTO, ITC). Panels deciding appeals/proceedings consist of at least three APJs or statutory members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte appeals eligibility (when to appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application is filed, if the examiner issues a rejection (including after twice rejecting the claims or issuing a 'final' office action), the applicant can seek review by the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process starts only after the requisite examiner actions (typically two rejections or a final action). This defines when an applicant may invoke ex parte appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte appeal procedural steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal begins with an 'appeal brief' filed by the appellant; the examiner files an 'answer'; the appellant may file a 'reply' (not always filed). A panel of at least three APJs (or statutory members) decides the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the core pleading stages in ex parte appeals; prepares parties for sequence and potential optional reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte appeal possible outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes may be an affirmance, an affirmance-in-part, a reversal, or new ground(s) of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided: Affirmance = rejection of each and every claim is upheld. Affirmance-in-part = rejection of at least one claim, but not all, is upheld. Reversal = none of the examiner's rejections are upheld. New ground(s) of rejection = Judges issue a new rejection of one or more claims. The outcome dictates who must take the next procedural step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of law and guidance for appeals and trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Governing authorities include U.S. Supreme Court and Federal Circuit decisions, 35 U.S.C. (Patents), 37 C.F.R. Part 41, precedential PTAB decisions, and Director guidance and memoranda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should rely on these authorities for legal standards and procedures in ex parte appeals and AIA proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA proceedings purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA proceedings are intended to increase the integrity of the patent system, act as an alternative vehicle for third parties to challenge patents via a streamlined, efficient, and cost-effective proceeding, be decided by administrative judges with expertise in complicated technology and areas of law, and provide fast resolutions of disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes policy goals underpinning IPR/PGR/Derivation procedures and expectations regarding speed and expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of AIA proceedings and core distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-Grant Review (PGR), Inter Partes Review (IPR), and Derivation: PGR has a limited 9-month window and broader range of challenges; IPR can be filed after 9 months and is limited to grounds under 35 U.S.C. § 102 or § 103 based on prior art patents or printed publications; Derivation has a 1-year window from claim publication and alleges another derived invention from the correct inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these distinctions to choose the correct proceeding and to understand timing and permissible grounds of challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an AIA petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Most people or corporate entities other than the patent owner can file a 'petition' (a petition fee is required). The U.S. government cannot. Certain people or corporations may be barred from filing based on actions they take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility constraints and fee requirement are important for determining standing and potential procedural bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties and burdens in AIA proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner (challenger) files the petition and carries the legal burden throughout the proceeding to prove claims are not patentable; the patent owner has opportunities to represent their interests; a panel of at least three APJs (or statutory members) decides the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies allocation of burdens and roles of participants during the trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA proceeding phases and statutory timeline constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: A proceeding has an institution phase and a trial phase with statutory timing controls; several procedural deadlines are specified (e.g., preliminary phase steps measured in months). Final written decision must be rendered no more than 12 months (by statute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slide shows a timing sequence with specific intervals: PO preliminary response (3 months), Petitioner opposition (2 months), PO request for discretionary denial (1 month), Director decision intervals, and trial-phase timing (3 months segments for PO resp. & MTA, Pet. reply & Opp. to MTA, etc.). Use the chart for detailed scheduling of filings and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common motions in AIA proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical motions include: pro hac vice admission; to seal; to exclude evidence; to amend claims; for additional discovery; to terminate; to strike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are frequent procedural requests practitioners should expect and plan for during trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory sources specific to AIA trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary authorities include 35 U.S.C. §§ 311-329 (statutes governing IPRs and PGRs) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.1-42.412 (rules/regulations for trials in general, and IPRs, PGRs, and Derivation Proceedings). Also: Consolidated Trial Practice Guide (Nov. 2019) and Director guidance and memoranda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite these when preparing petitions, responses, motions, and when evaluating procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Federal Rules of Evidence and Civil Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Rules of Evidence apply in proceedings expressly by regulation (37 C.F.R. § 42.62) — e.g., motions to exclude evidence and expert testimony. The Federal Rules of Civil Procedure do not apply; the Board has its own rules on discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume FRCP discovery or procedures apply; follow Board-specific discovery rules and the limited incorporation of FRE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible outcomes in final written decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Final written decisions may: uphold all challenged claims (each and every challenged claim upheld); be mixed (at least one challenged claim, but not all, upheld); or hold all claims unpatentable (no challenged claim upheld).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine post-decision options and implications for appeals or further actions based on which outcome occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-final-decision options
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may seek a panel rehearing, seek review of the Board’s decision by the Director of the USPTO ('Director Review'), or appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the principal avenues for challenging or seeking further consideration of a final written decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB institutional priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB priorities include: execute all duties as required under 35 U.S.C. § 6; maintain high decisional quality; reduce pendency of ex parte appeals; meet all statutory deadlines in AIA proceedings; and implement IT improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows administrative priorities that may affect resourcing, pendency, and institutional initiatives relevant to practitioners.
